children: The following bids, mergers, acquisitions and disposals were reported by 2020 GMT on Tuesday:
** A consortium led by Italy's Treasury remains committed to buying Telecom Italia
's submarine cable unit, the telecoms group said after a deadline to close the deal passed pending a required approval from US regulators.
** SpaceX
shareholders want to know when the rocket maker will merge with Tesla
, bringing together two of Elon Musk's biggest companies in a union that investors have long speculated about.
** Blackstone Inc
and Warburg Pincus are exploring a sale of IntraFi that could value the financial technology company at more than $10 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.
** Brazilian steelmaker CSN
continues to conduct a competitive process for the sale of its cement business, the company said in a securities filing.
** Salesforce
is buying Braze
in a deal valued at about $5.66 billion, bolstering its AI push with tools that let brands send personalized messages and respond to customer behavior in real time.
** Prudential Financial
said it would sell its Brazil and Mexico units to French insurance group CNP Assurances Group for $4.03 billion in cash as part of its ongoing push to simplify its business.
** Gulf Keystone Petroleum
said it would merge with Norway's ShaMaran Petroleum
in a $601 million all-share 50-50 deal, creating one of the largest producers in Iraq's oil-rich Kurdistan region.
** Italy's second-largest bank, UniCredit
, said it was bringing its domestic securities services unit back in-house, two decades after outsourcing the business to Societe Generale
** Italian engineering group Maire
said its Nextchem unit had signed binding agreements to buy Swedish MEAB AB and German MEAB GmbH for a maximum amount of €8 million ($9 million).
** Singapore's Keppel
said it would sell a 51% stake in K-Commercial, the entity that owns the Keppel South Central office building, to Keppel REIT
for about S$611 million ($477.42 million).
** Tradeweb Markets
said on Monday it will buy bond-trading platform Trumid for about $1.97 billion, as it seeks to expand its presence in US corporate bond markets.
